source.title: The orbit method and analysis of automorphic forms
source.authors: Paul D. Nelson and Akshay Venkatesh
source.version: The published Acta text (open-access International Press PDF, 209 pages, created 30 March 2021), read in full; locators and page numbers are the published ones. arXiv v3 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.07750v3, 7 January 2021, SHA-256 9bce49cb7d3f6f2f6994c7af0ecbf3f12c3e4f79599091543d331824f522c03e) was compared at every finding. Pages 42, 50, 128, 130, 166 and 182 were checked on page images. This extraction continues the partial checkpoint of cc-d67081 (#2214, arXiv v3, theorem statements only), keeping its route ids; items note the arXiv v3 theorem numbers and the checkpoint ids they supersede.

summary: Nelson and Venkatesh develop the orbit method quantitatively: a microlocal calculus Op_h on unitary representations of Lie groups, with symbol classes, composition, localization and trace estimates coming from the Kirillov formula (Parts I–II). They study Gan–Gross–Prasad pairs (stability ⇔ no conductor drop; stable fibres are H-torsors; volume-form identities) and prove asymptotics for relative characters away from the conductor-dropping locus (Part III). They solve inverse branching problems at archimedean and p-adic places (Part IV). With limit states, Ratner's theorem and a truncated spectral expansion, they show that for a fixed generic tempered Π on an anisotropic GGP pair, the branching coefficients L(Π, Σ) average to 1/τ(G) = 1/2 over families of Σ with growing archimedean parameter; under Ichino–Ikeda/N. Harris this is an average of central L-values in arbitrarily large rank, with a weak subconvex bound (Part V). The atlas has none of this and neither library has coadjoint orbits or unitary representation calculi. Routes, as in cc-d67081's checkpoint (#2214): the machinery to a new roadmap, QuantitativeOrbitMethodAndMicrolocalAnalysisOnLieGroups, and the automorphic statements to the proposed GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups; After the red team (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21), seven further routes, appended after the reviewed ones, send the real Langlands classification to AF.1, the real Plancherel formula to the AutomorphicSpectralTheory Part II, Lemma 23.4 to SR.3, affine GIT to the Reductive algebraic groups Part II, Ratner and Borel density to GN.4, the reductive Harish-Chandra isomorphism to a LieHighestWeight Part II, and the Schwartz kernel theorem to AS.0. Complete (cc-442dc5), superseding that partial checkpoint; its item ids are mapped in the notes. Main findings: Theorem 27.1 and the main theorem are false for (SO3, SO2) when Π is dihedral for the torus's quadratic field (the proof of Lemma 27.3 fails there; the weak subconvex bound survives); a gap in the non-stationary-phase proof (Lemma 7.8); an invalid example after Lemma 24.10; a wrong citation for the orthogonal non-vanishing result; a missing O(h^N) in Theorem 22.2(iii); misprints, and slips copied into items, corrected after the red team. Not formalised.

items.name: Schwartz spaces and Fourier inversion on the Lie algebra
items.statement: With dx a Haar measure on g and dξ the dual measure on g^∧ ≅ ig*, φ ↦ φ^∧(ξ) = ∫ φ(x)e^{xξ}dx and a ↦ a^∨(x) = ∫ a(ξ)e^{−xξ}dξ are mutually inverse isomorphisms S(g) ≅ S(g^∧).
items.note: Mathlib's Schwartz space and its Fourier transform with inversion on a finite-dimensional real inner product space (082e2d3); the paper's pairing e^{xξ}, ξ ∈ ig*, is a change of normalisation. (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) schwartz-space.) Corrected by cc-7b31c4: SchwartzMap.fourierTransformCLE does not exist at 082e2d3 — the name occurs only in the module docstring of Mathlib/Analysis/Distribution/SchwartzSpace/Fourier.lean, which promises the transform 'also given as a continuous linear equiv'. Inversion on Schwartz space is SchwartzMap.instFourierTransform (Fourier.lean:86), whose fourierInv_fourier_eq and fourier_fourierInv_eq are proved there, with the general statements Continuous.fourierInv_fourier_eq and MeasureTheory.Integrable.fourierInv_fourier_eq in Analysis/Fourier/Inversion.lean.

items.name: The operator assignment Op and its rescaling Op_h
items.statement: For a small even neighbourhood G of 0 in g on which exp is an analytic isomorphism, a cut-off χ ∈ X(G) (even, [0,1]-valued, ≡ 1 near 0), a unitary representation π of the unimodular Lie group G and a ∈ S(g^∧): Op(a, χ : π) = ∫_g χ(x)a^∨(x)π(exp x)dx and Op_h(a, χ) = Op(a_h, χ) = ∫ χ(hx)a^∨(x)π(exp(hx))dx, a_h(ξ) = a(hξ). Op(a, χ)* = Op(ā, χ), and π(g)Op(a, χ)π(g)⁻¹ = Op(g·a, g·χ) when Ad(g)supp(χ) ⊆ G.
items.note: (2.1)–(2.2), §§2.3–2.4. (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) operator-assignment.)

items.name: The star product and the composition formula
items.statement: With x∗y = log(exp x exp y) on G×G ⊆ G′ and χ′ ≡ 1 on supp χ ∗ supp χ, the star product a1⋆a2 = (χa1^∨ ⋆ χa2^∨)^∧ (group convolution pulled back to g) satisfies Op(a1, χ)Op(a2, χ) = Op(a1⋆a2, χ′), and Op_h(a, χ)Op_h(b, χ) = Op_h(a⋆_h b, χ′) with (a⋆_h b)_h = a_h⋆b_h.
items.note: §2.5, p. 28, prints Op for Op_h in the rescaled formula (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E18). (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) star-product.)

items.name: Sobolev spaces and operator classes Ψ^m
items.statement: ∆ = 1 − Σ_{x∈B} x² (B a basis of g) is positive self-adjoint with ‖∆⁻¹‖ ≤ 1; π^s is the completion of π^∞ for ⟨v1, v2⟩_{π^s} = ⟨∆^s v1, v2⟩. An operator T: π^∞ → π^{−∞} has order ≤ m if θ_u(T) = [π(x1), [..., [π(xn), T]]] is bounded π^s → π^{s−m} for all s ∈ Z and u ∈ U; Ψ^m, Ψ^{−∞} = ∩Ψ^m and Ψ^∞ = ∪Ψ^m carry the evident topologies.

items.name: Composition and basic members of the operator classes
items.statement: Composition gives continuous maps Ψ^{m1} × Ψ^{m2} → Ψ^{m1+m2} (Lemma 3.3); π(∆)^m ∈ Ψ^{2m} and π(x1…xm) ∈ Ψ^m (Lemma 3.4); T ∈ Ψ^{−∞} iff every ∆^N T ∆^N is bounded (Lemma 3.5); π(f) ∈ Ψ^{−∞} continuously for f ∈ C_c^∞(G) (Lemma 3.6).
items.note: Lemmas 3.3–3.6; Lemma 3.4 is proved in the general form of Proposition 8.6.

items.name: Symbol classes S^m and S^m_δ
items.statement: S^m: smooth a on g^∧ with |∂^α a(ξ)| ≤ C_α⟨ξ⟩^{m−|α|}; S^{−∞} = S(g^∧). For δ ∈ [0,1), S^m_δ: smooth h-dependent a with |∂^α a(ξ)| ≤ C_α h^{−δ|α|}⟨ξ⟩^{m−|α|} uniformly in h ∈ (0,1]; h^η S^m_δ is the rescaled class.
items.note: Definitions 4.1 and 4.3, §4.5. (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) symbol-classes.)

items.name: Asymptotics of the star product
items.statement: (i) ⋆ extends uniquely to continuous S^∞ × S^∞ → S^∞, S^{m1} × S^{m2} → S^{m1+m2}, and for δ ∈ [0, 1/2), ⋆_h: S^{m1}_δ × S^{m2}_δ → S^{m1+m2}_δ. (ii) a⋆b ≡ Σ_{j<J} a⋆^j b mod S^{m1+m2−J} and a⋆_h b ≡ Σ_{j<J} h^j a⋆^j b mod h^{(1−2δ)J} S^{m1+m2−J}_δ with continuously varying remainder, where ⋆^j is the bidifferential operator (4.5) from the BCH remainder {x,y} = x∗y − x − y; a⋆^0 b = ab and a⋆^1 b is a multiple of the Poisson bracket.
items.note: With (4.2)–(4.6), (4.10)–(4.11); proved as Theorem 7.4. (arXiv v3 Theorem 1; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-1.)

items.name: Polynomial symbols
items.statement: For p ∈ Sym(g_C), viewed as a polynomial on g^∧, Op(p, χ) = π(sym(p)), sym the symmetrisation map; in particular Op(⟨ξ⟩²) = ∆ for an orthonormal basis.
items.note: Proved in §8.1.

items.name: h-dependent operator classes Ψ^m_δ
items.statement: For h-dependent π, Ψ^m_δ consists of h-dependent T with ‖h^{nδ}θ_{x1…xn}(T)‖_{π^s→π^{s−m}} bounded uniformly in h; h^∞Ψ^m = ∩_η h^ηΨ^m_δ. Lemma 5.3: h-uniformly continuous seminorms on Ψ^m are O(h^{−M}) on Ψ^m_δ, and continuous functionals on Ψ^{−N} restrict continuously to Ψ^{−N′}_δ.
items.note: Definition 5.2 and Lemma 5.3.

items.name: Independence of the cut-off
items.statement: For χ1, χ2 ∈ X(G): Op(a, χ1) ≡ Op(a, χ2) mod Ψ^{−∞} for a ∈ S^∞, and Op_h(a, χ1) ≡ Op_h(a, χ2) mod h^∞Ψ^{−∞} for a ∈ S^∞_δ, with continuously varying remainder.

items.name: Near-equivariance
items.statement: For δ ∈ [0,1), ε > 0 and h-dependent g ∈ G with ‖Ad(g)‖ ≪ h^{−1+δ+ε}: Op_h(g·a) ≡ π(g)Op_h(a)π(g)⁻¹ mod h^∞Ψ^{−∞} for a ∈ S^∞_δ.

items.name: Op maps symbols to operators, compatibly with composition
items.statement: Op(S^m) ⊆ Ψ^m continuously for m ∈ Z ∪ {±∞}, and Op(a)Op(b) = Op(a⋆b, χ′) ≡ Op(a⋆b) mod Ψ^{−∞}; hence Op(a)Op(b) ≡ Σ_{j<J} Op(a⋆^j b) mod Ψ^{m1+m2−J} (Corollary 5.7).
items.note: Theorem 5.6 and Corollary 5.7; proved in §8.7. (arXiv v3 Theorem 2; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-2.)

items.name: The rescaled calculus
items.statement: For δ ∈ [0, 1/2) and m ∈ Z, Op_h(S^m_δ) ⊆ h^{min(0,m)}Ψ^m_δ, and Op_h(a)Op_h(b) ≡ Op_h(a⋆_h b) mod h^∞Ψ^{−∞}; for M, N there is J with Op_h(a)Op_h(b) ≡ Σ_{j<J} h^j Op_h(a⋆^j b) mod h^NΨ^{−M}_δ (Corollary 5.9).
items.note: Theorem 5.8 and Corollary 5.9; proved in §8.8. (arXiv v3 Theorem 3; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-3.)

items.name: Coadjoint orbits, normalized symplectic measure and multiorbits
items.statement: A coadjoint orbit O ⊆ g^∧ carries σ_ξ(ad*_xξ, ad*_yξ) = [x,y]ξ/i and ω_O = (1/d!)(σ/2π)^d, d = ½dim O; ∫_O f dω_O = t^{−d}∫_{tO} f(t⁻¹x)dω_{tO} (6.1). A (regular) coadjoint multiorbit is a finite union of (regular) orbits with one infinitesimal character; their number per infinitesimal character is bounded in terms of G.
items.note: (6.1) is printed for f ∈ C_c^∞(g); read g^∧ (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E8). (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) coadjoint-multiorbit.)

items.name: The Kirillov character formula (Rossmann; cited)
items.statement: For G real reductive and π tempered irreducible there is a unique non-empty regular coadjoint multiorbit O_π ⊆ g^∧ with χ_π(e^x)√j(x) = ∫_{O_π} e^{xξ}dω(ξ) as distributions near 0; its infinitesimal character is that of π, and it is a single orbit if λ_π is regular.
items.note: Rossmann [Ros1, Ros2, Ros4]; Harish-Chandra's locally L¹ character χ_π is an input. (arXiv v3 Theorem 4; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-4.)

items.name: Trace estimates for the calculus
items.statement: For N large: (i) tr(Op_h(a)) = h^{−d}(∫_{hO_π} a dω_{hO_π} + O(h)) for a ∈ S^{−N}, uniformly in tempered π; (ii) every T ∈ Ψ^{−N}(π) is trace class, continuously and uniformly in π; (iii) h^d Op_h(a) has bounded trace norm for a ∈ S^{−N}_δ, δ < 1/2.
items.note: With (6.3)–(6.4) and Remarks 6.4–6.6; refined in Theorem 12.2. (arXiv v3 Theorem 5; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-5.)

items.name: Star products for pairs of subalgebras
items.statement: For Lie subalgebras g1, g2 ⊆ g with g1 + g2 = g (of unimodular subgroups), ⋆: S(g1^∧) × S(g2^∧) → S(g^∧) extends uniquely to continuous S^{m1}(g1^∧) × S^{m2}(g2^∧) → S^{m1+m2}(g^∧) for admissible (m1, m2) (m2 = −∞ if g1 ≠ g, m1 = −∞ if g2 ≠ g); for δ1 + δ2 < 1, a⋆_h b ≡ Σ_{j<J} h^j a⋆^j b mod h^{(1−δ1−δ2)J} S^{m1+m2−J}_{max δ}(g^∧).
items.note: With Example 7.1, Definition 7.2 and Lemma 7.3. (arXiv v3 Theorem 6; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-6.)

items.name: Taylor bound for the BCH phase
items.statement: With Ω(x,y,ζ) = e^{{x,y}ζ} = Σ_j Ω_j and ρ = max(|x|, |y|, |x||y||ζ|): ∂_ζ^δ(Ω − Σ_{j<J}Ω_j) ≪ ρ^J on G1 × G2 × g^∧.
items.note: The printed intermediate bound (7.4) is not right for ρ < 1 (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E4).

items.name: Non-stationary phase
items.statement: If φ: Ω → iR is smooth on Ω ⊆ R^n with |∂φ| ≥ ε, then |∫ f e^{tφ}| ≪ t^{−N} Σ_{|α|≤N} ‖∂^α f‖_{L¹} for f ∈ C_c^∞(Ω), t > 0, continuously in φ; consequently ∂^γ_ζF(ξ, η, ζ) ≪ t^{−N} when t = |(ξ, η)| ≥ ½|ζ|.
items.note: Lemmas 7.7–7.8; the printed proof has a gap (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E2).

items.name: Localized symbols and dyadic–Planck partitions
items.statement: a ∈ S^m_δ is localized at ω if supported on U_ω = {|ξ − ω| ≤ ½h^δ⟨ω⟩}; then a(ξ) = ⟨ω⟩^m φ((ξ−ω)/(h^δ⟨ω⟩)) and a_h^∨(x) = ⟨ω⟩^m e^{−xω/h}A^{dim g}φ^∨(Ax), A = h^{δ−1}⟨ω⟩. There is an h-dependent Ω ⊆ g^∧ with bounded overlaps, polynomial counting and a partition of unity, so every a ∈ S^m_δ is Σ_ω ⟨ω⟩^m a_ω with a_ω ∈ S^0_δ localized.
items.note: Definition 7.9, Lemmas 7.10–7.12 (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E10).

items.name: Remainder estimates for localized star products
items.statement: For δ1 + δ2 < 1 and a ∈ S^0_{δ1}(g1^∧), b ∈ S^0_{δ2}(g2^∧) localized at ω1, ω2, the remainder r = a⋆_h b − Σ_{j<J} h^j a⋆^j b satisfies ∂^γ r(ζ) ≪ h^N⟨ζ⟩^{−N} times ⟨ω1⟩^{±}, ⟨ω2⟩^{±} factors as in cases (a)–(d), uniformly in ω1, ω2.

items.name: Asymptotics for convolution with a bump
items.statement: For ψ ∈ C_c^∞(g) and a ∈ S^m_δ, the b with b_h^∨ = ψa_h^∨ lies in S^m_δ and b ≡ Σ_{j<J} h^j Σ_{|α|=j} (∂^αψ(0)/α!) ∂^α a mod h^{(1−δ)J}S^{m−J}_δ.
items.note: The paper prints (−h)^j; under its convention (4.1) the coefficient is h^j (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E19).

items.name: Fourier transforms of symbols away from the origin
items.statement: For a ∈ S^∞, a^∨ is smooth off 0 with ∂^α a^∨(x) ≪ |x|^{−N} when |α| + m − N ≤ −dim g − 1, and ∂^α a_h^∨(x) ≪ h^{−dim g−|α|}|x/h^{1−δ}|^{−N} for a ∈ S^m_δ; a^∨ is n-times differentiable at 0 if m ≤ −dim g − 1 − n.
items.note: (8.3) as printed omits the factor h^{−|α|} (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E17).

items.name: Membership criterion for Ψ^m
items.statement: T ∈ Ψ^m iff for every u ∈ U: sup ‖θ_u(T)v‖²/⟨∆^m v, v⟩ < ∞ (m ≥ 0), or sup ‖θ_u(T)x1…x_{−m}v‖/‖v‖ < ∞ over x_i ∈ {1} ∪ B (m ≤ 0); and π(t) ∈ Ψ^m for every t ∈ U[∆⁻¹] of order ≤ m (Proposition 8.6).
items.note: Proposition 8.2, Definition 8.3, Lemmas 8.4–8.5, Proposition 8.6.

items.name: L²-boundedness of order-zero operators
items.statement: Op(a) is bounded on π for a ∈ S^0, and Op_h(a) is bounded uniformly in h for a ∈ S^0_δ, δ < 1/2, with norm controlled continuously by a and uniformly in π.
items.note: Via ‖Op_h(a)‖ ≤ ‖a^∨‖_{L¹} (Lemma 8.8), Lemma 8.9 and the Cotlar–Stein lemma.

items.name: The Cotlar–Stein lemma (cited)
items.statement: If T_j: V1 → V2 satisfy sup_j Σ_k ‖T_j*T_k‖^{1/2} ≤ C and sup_j Σ_k ‖T_jT_k*‖^{1/2} ≤ C, then Σ_j T_j converges strongly (in the strong operator topology) to T with ‖T‖ ≤ C.
items.note: [Hör, Lemma 18.6.5]; not in the pinned libraries. The paper says the series converges in the Banach space of bounded operators, which is false (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E16); its use needs only strong convergence and the bound.

items.name: Composition across proper subgroups
items.statement: For admissible (m1, m2), δ < 1/2, a ∈ S^{m1}_δ(g1^∧), b ∈ S^{m2}_δ(g2^∧): Op_h(a)Op_h(b) = Op_h(a⋆_h b) ≡ Σ_{j<J} h^j Op_h(a⋆^j b) mod h^NΨ^{−M}_δ; if the preimages in g^∧ of supp a and supp b are disjoint, Op_h(a)Op_h(b) ∈ h^∞Ψ^{−∞} continuously (Lemma 8.12).
items.note: Theorem 8.11 and Lemma 8.12. (arXiv v3 Theorem 7; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-7.)

items.name: The Harish-Chandra isomorphism for semisimple g_C
items.statement: For g_C semisimple, Harish-Chandra's γ: Z(U(g_C)) ≅ S(t_C)^W (γ(z) the ρ-shifted projection along (9.4)).
items.note: LieHighestWeight layer 7 builds Z(U(L)) ≅ S(H)^{W·} for Killing-semisimple split L only. The paper's groups include U(n) and GL_n: Chevalley's restriction theorem and the reductive isomorphism are /102, and the real form [ig*] with λ_π is /103 (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/10). AF.1 plans only U(g_C) and its centre action.

items.name: Infinitesimal characters of duals and conjugates
items.statement: λ_{π*} = −λ_π, λ_{π̄} = λ̄_π and λ_{π⁺} = −λ̄_π; hence λ_π ∈ [ig*] for irreducible unitary π (Corollary 9.3).
items.note: Lemma 9.2 and Corollary 9.3.

items.name: The Langlands classification (cited)
items.statement: Each irreducible π is the unique irreducible quotient of i^G_P σ for a unique conjugacy class of (P, σ) with σ tempered on the derived group of M and |central character| strictly dominant; λ_σ maps to λ_π under [m*_C] → [g*_C].
items.note: [Kn, Theorem 8.54, Proposition 8.22]. Routed (route 3) to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.1, the owner of real reductive representation theory; AF.1b takes it once the RT-AREA-automorphic-1 fixes are applied. PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21/20(b) plans the same classification and should import it from there. Route 1 imports it.

items.name: Infinitesimal criterion for temperedness
items.statement: For compact Ω ⊆ [ig*]_reg there is h0 > 0 such that every irreducible unitary π with hλ_π ∈ Ω, 0 < h < h0, is tempered.

items.name: Eigenvalues of ∆ and infinitesimal characters
items.statement: ∆ has an eigenvalue of size O(1 + |λ_π|²) on each irreducible unitary π (via ∆ = 2∆_K − 1 − C, Vogan's minimal K-types and Blattner's formula); and γ∘sym(p) − p has order ≤ n − 1 for p ∈ Sym(g_C)^G of order ≤ n (Lemma 9.6).
items.note: Lemmas 9.5–9.6 and the norms of §9.8.

items.name: Approximate division
items.statement: For δ1, δ2 < 1/2, a ∈ S^{−∞}_{δ1} and q ∈ S^∞_0 with |q| ≥ h^{δ2} on supp a, there are b, b′ ∈ h^{−δ2}S^{−∞}_δ with Op_h(a) ≡ Op_h(q)Op_h(b) ≡ Op_h(b′)Op_h(q) mod h^NΨ^{−M}_δ.

items.name: Localizing near the locus of a symbol
items.statement: If H: Ψ^{−∞} → C is h-uniformly continuous and H(Op_h(p)T) = λH(T) (or H(T Op_h(p)) = λH(T)), then H(Op_h(a)) ≪ h^{−M}⟨λ⟩^{−N}, and ≪ h^N⟨λ⟩^{−N} if |p − λ| ≥ h^δ on supp a.

items.name: Localizing near infinitesimal characters
items.statement: If H: Ψ^{−∞}(π) → C factors (H × H)-equivariantly through Ψ^{−∞}(σ) → C, then H(Op_h(a)) ≪ h^{−M}⟨hλ_π⟩^{−N}⟨hλ_σ⟩^{−N}, and ≪ h^N⟨hλ_π⟩^{−N}⟨hλ_σ⟩^{−N} if a is supported off {ξ: dist([ξ], hλ_π) ≤ h^δ, dist([ξ|_h], hλ_σ) ≤ h^δ}.
items.note: The proof's (10.12), (10.14) write p(hλ_σ) for every p (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E13).

items.name: Topology on regular coadjoint multiorbits (after Rossmann)
items.statement: Topologise regular multiorbits by weak-* convergence of ω_O. If O_j has a non-empty limit it is the set O of regular limits of points ξ_j ∈ O_j; conversely if O ≠ ∅ contains all regular subsequential limits, O_j → O. (Lemmas 11.2–11.3: λ ↦ ω_λ and ξ ↦ ω_{G·ξ}|_U vary continuously.)
items.note: Theorem 11.1 with Lemmas 11.2–11.3 [Ros2, Ros3]. (arXiv v3 Theorem 8; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-8.)

items.name: Uniform bounds for symplectic measures
items.statement: sup_O |∫_O a dω| < ∞ for a ∈ C_c(g^∧), and sup_O ⟨[O]⟩^ε ∫_O ⟨ξ⟩^{−d(O)−ε}dω_O < ∞, over non-empty regular multiorbits.

items.name: Limit orbits of fixed representations
items.statement: An h-dependent tempered π has limit orbit O if hO_π → O. A fixed tempered π has a limit orbit O ⊆ N_reg, and O ≠ ∅ ⇔ π has maximal Gelfand–Kirillov dimension ⇔ π is generic (G quasi-split, Whittaker model).
items.note: §11.4.1 and Lemma 11.6 [BV, Ros5, Kos3, Cas1].

items.name: Refined trace estimates
items.statement: For even N > d and tempered h-dependent π: tr(Op_h(a)) ≪ h^{−d}⟨hλ_π⟩^{d−N}; h^d tr(Op_h(a)) = ∫_{hO_π} a dω + O(h^{1−δ}⟨hλ_π⟩^{d−N−1}) and = Σ_{j<J} h^j ∫_{hO_π} D_j a dω + O(h^{(1−δ)J}) for constant-coefficient D_j of degree j; lim h^d tr(Op_h(a)) = ∫_O a dω under a limit orbit; ∆_h^{−N/2} is trace class with norm ≍ h^{−d}⟨hλ_π⟩^{d−N}; ‖T‖_1 ≤ C⟨λ_π⟩^{d−N}‖T‖_{π^0→π^N}; Op_h(S^{−N}_0) ⊆ h^{−d}⟨hλ_π⟩^{d−N}T_1; products and conjugates as in (12.7)–(12.9).
items.note: With §12.1 (classes T_p) and Lemma 12.1 (approximate inverse of ∆_h). (arXiv v3 Theorem 9; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-9.)

items.name: Uniform bounds for K-types and matrix coefficients
items.statement: There is κ ∈ U(k) acting by κ_τ on τ ∈ K̂ with dim τ ≤ κ_τ^{1/2} and Σκ_τ⁻¹ < ∞; for F archimedean and π irreducible admissible, dim(Kv)^{1/2}‖v‖ ≤ ‖κv‖ for τ-isotypic v, and tr π(κ)⁻² ≤ C. With the Harish-Chandra function Ξ, |⟨gu, v⟩| ≤ cΞ(g)‖u‖_{π^s}‖v‖_{π^s} for tempered π (Lemma A.2, from Cowling–Haagerup–Howe).
items.note: Lemmas A.1–A.2 and (A.1) [CHH]. Lemma A.1(i) is for τ-isotypic v; for general v the inequality fails (a principal series of SL₂(R), with small components in many K-types). The explicit κ = −cΣx² suggested on p. 136 does not satisfy (ii); a power (1 − Σx²)^N does (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E24).

items.name: Uniform trace-class property of ∆^{−N}
items.statement: For N large in terms of G: sup_π tr π(∆^{−N}) < ∞ over the unitary dual, and ∫_{tempered} tr π(∆^{−N}) < ∞ for Plancherel measure.

items.name: Gan–Gross–Prasad pairs
items.statement: For k of characteristic 0, k1 ∈ {k, a quadratic field, k × k} with involution ι, and (V, ⟨,⟩) a non-degenerate ι-symmetric k1-form, G = Aut(V/k1, ⟨,⟩)⁰ ⊆ GL(V); for e with ⟨e,e⟩ ≠ 0 and V_H = (k1e)^⊥, H = Aut(V_H)⁰ ↪ G. A GGP pair is such an inclusion with its standard representations: (SO_n, SO_{n+1}), (U_n, U_{n+1}) or (GL_n, GL_{n+1}) forms.
items.note: §§13.1–13.3, (III.1). (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) ggp-pair.)

items.name: Eigenvalue invariants ev(x)
items.statement: The coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of x ∈ g (skew-adjoint) generate the invariant ring, with the Pfaffian added in the even orthogonal case; ev(x) is the multiset of eigenvalues on V⁺ (minus one zero in the odd orthogonal case) and [x] ↦ (ev(x), pf(x)) or ev(x) is injective on [g].

items.name: Eigenvalues and isotropic eigenvectors; a regularity criterion
items.statement: c ∈ ev(x) ⇔ x has an isotropic eigenvector in V⁺ with eigenvalue c ⇔ one in V⁻ with eigenvalue −c (Lemma 13.1). If every isotropic subspace of V⁺ on which x is scalar has dimension ≤ 1 (and, orthogonally, dim ker x ≤ 2), x is regular (Lemma 13.2).

items.name: GGP pairs are spherical (cited)
items.statement: H has an open orbit with trivial stabilizer on the flag variety of G × H (H embedded diagonally).

items.name: GIT stability background (cited)
items.statement: For reductive H acting on affine M over algebraically closed k: M//H is affine, φ: M → M//H surjective and universal; the H-stable locus M^s (finite stabilizer, closed orbit) and φ(M^s) are open, and if stabilizers on M^s are trivial then M^s → φ(M^s) is a principal H-bundle (étale locally trivial). Hilbert–Mumford: x is not H-stable iff some non-trivial cocharacter has only non-negative weights on x (for M a representation of H, as in the applications).
items.note: [MFK, Proposition 0.9], [Mi]; §14.1.1 moment-map form of finiteness; (14.2). 'Not H-stable', not 'unstable': in the null-cone sense the statement is false (G_m acting trivially on A¹, x = 1). The stability form follows from the closed-orbit form (Richardson, Kempf) with Matsushima's theorem. Routed (route 6) to the Part II of Tau Ceti's Reductive algebraic groups that PAPER-FINTZEN-21 route 4 proposes (pending as DESIGN-ReductiveGroupsPartIII), which plans semistability and Kempf's cocharacter (FINTZEN-21 /32, /32a); PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19/4 and PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18/35 send the categorical quotient and Hilbert–Mumford to LanglandsParameterStacks LP2/LP3, and one owner must be chosen. Route 1 imports it.

items.name: Stability for GGP pairs
items.statement: For x ∈ g: x is H-stable ⇔ ev(x) ∩ ev(x_H) = ∅ (x_H = ExE on V_H) ⇔ x has no isotropic eigenvector in V_H⁺ ∪ V_H⁻ ⇔ k1[x]e is all of V (unitary) or a non-degenerate subspace of codimension ≤ 1 (orthogonal). A pair (λ, µ) ∈ [g]×[h] is stable if ev(λ) ∩ ev(µ) = ∅; stable pairs are dense open.
items.note: Theorem 14.2, Definition 14.3, Lemmas 14.4 and 14.8; Remark 14.9 compares Rallis–Schiffmann and notes an inaccuracy there (footnote 5). (arXiv v3 Theorem 10; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-10.)

items.name: Stable fibres are H-torsors
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0 (§14.3): x ↦ ([x], [x_H]) from the H-stable locus of g onto the stable pairs in [g]×[h] is a principal H-bundle; each fibre O^{λ,µ} is an H-torsor. The map g → [g]×[h] is surjective, and stable x has x, x_H regular. Over R (Theorem 17.1) a fibre is empty or an H-torsor.
items.note: Theorem 14.5 with Lemmas 14.6–14.7; uses (14.8). §14.3 assumes k algebraically closed: over R both conclusions fail on points (for compact (SO(3), SO(2)), stable pairs (A, b) with b² > A have no real preimage). (arXiv v3 Theorem 11; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-11.)

items.name: Infinitesimal characters and Langlands parameters
items.statement: Over R: for π with Langlands parameter φ_π, φ_π|_{C*}(e^t) = exp(tλ_π + t̄µ_π) (µ_π = −λ̄_π if π tempered), and under g^∨//G^∨ ≅ [g*_C] the element λ_π is the infinitesimal character of π.

items.name: Satake parameters of the Rankin–Selberg L-function
items.statement: Over R (K = R, §15.2): for the Rankin–Selberg representation ρ of L(H × G) (dimensions (2n−2)·2n, (2n)², 2n(n−1)), the eigenvalues of ρ(A^∨ × B^∨) are (ev(A′) + ev(B′)) × {±1} (unitary) or × {1} (orthogonal); so, for π and σ tempered, L_R(π × σ, ρ, s) = ∏ Γ_R(s + λ_i⁺ + ε_i) over these parameters.
items.note: §§15.2–15.4. (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) satake-and-l-functions.)

items.name: Stability is absence of conductor dropping
items.statement: Over R: for π, σ with infinitesimal characters λ, µ: (λ, µ) is stable ⇔ no Satake parameter of L(π × σ^∨, ρ, s) is zero.

items.name: Fibral, Haar, symplectic and affine volume forms
items.statement: A smooth X → Y → Z with volume forms β on Y, γ on Z gives the fibral form α = β/γ; Haar forms on h*; the symplectic volume form σ^d/d! on each regular orbit O^µ_reg (the unique open orbit in its fibre, Kostant); and affine forms dp1 ∧ … ∧ dpr on [h*], with (16.3) its pull-back ∏_{α>0}⟨µ, α^∨⟩ ∧H_i.
items.note: Lemma 16.2 [Kos2]; Examples 16.1, 16.3.

items.name: The normalized affine form
items.statement: For each Haar form β_H on h* there is a unique affine form γ_H on [h*] such that for every µ the fibral form of O^µ_reg → h* → [h*] is the symplectic volume form.
items.note: [Ros2, Lemma C]; Definition 16.5, Remark 16.6.

items.name: Compatibility of orbital volume forms
items.statement: For Haar forms β_G, β_H, normalized affine forms γ_G, γ_H and stable (λ, µ), the orbital volume form α on O^{λ,µ} (transported from H) is, up to sign, the fibral volume form in each of the three sequences of (16.4): O^{λ,µ} → O^λ_reg × O^{−µ}_reg → h*, O^{λ,µ} → O^λ_reg → [h*], and O^{λ,µ} → g*_reg → [g*] × [h*].
items.note: Proofs in §16.5.1 (Lagrangian fibration) and §16.5.2 (spherical degeneration). (arXiv v3 Theorem 12; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-12.)

items.name: Measure normalizations over R
items.statement: |dx| = Lebesgue/√(2π) on A¹ (self-dual for e^{ix}); dx on g compatible with dg, dξ its Fourier dual, β with |β| = dξ, |ω_alg| = ω, and the normalized affine measure |γ| on [g^∧], giving ∫_{g^∧} a = ∫_{[g^∧]}∫_{O^λ_reg} a dω (17.2).

items.name: Stable fibres over R and the disintegration formulas
items.statement: g^∧_stab → {stable (λ, µ)} is a principal H-bundle over its image with fibres O^{λ,µ} (empty or H-torsors of stable regular elements); for regular multiorbits O, O(µ) and O_{π,σ} = O_π(λ_σ) = O^{λ_π,λ_σ} when (λ_π, λ_σ) is stable and O_{π,σ} is non-empty. Integration over O^{λ,µ} (Haar transported from H) is continuous in (λ, µ, a), and ∫_{O^λ_reg} a dω = ∫_{[h^∧]} ∫_{O^{λ,µ}} a, more generally ∫_O a dω = ∫_{[h^∧]}∫_{O(µ)} a.
items.note: Theorems 17.1–17.2 and (17.3)–(17.5). Without non-emptiness (17.3) fails: for (U(1,1), U(1)) and a holomorphic discrete series π, O^{λ_π,µ} can be a non-empty U(1)-torsor while O_{π,σ} = ∅. (arXiv v3 Theorem 14; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-13, theorem-14.)

items.name: A Łojasiewicz-type inequality
items.statement: For H-stable ξ there are c1, c2 > 0 and a neighbourhood U of ξ with |s·η| > c1|s|^{c2} for all η ∈ U, s ∈ H.

items.name: Plancherel measure and affine measure
items.statement: For a complex group and a non-empty bounded open U ⊆ [h^∧] with null boundary, (Plancherel measure of {σ tempered: λ_σ ∈ h⁻¹U}) / (normalized affine measure of h⁻¹U) → 1 as h → 0.
items.note: Sketched via the Plancherel and Kirillov formulas (§17.5).

items.name: Relative characters
items.statement: For a GGP pair over a local field and tempered π, σ, H_σ(v1 ⊗ v̄2) = Σ_{u∈B(σ)}∫_H⟨sv1, v2⟩⟨u, su⟩ (the local period of /101 summed over an orthonormal basis B(σ) of K_H-isotypic vectors) converges to an H-invariant Hermitian form, tr(T) = ∫_{Ĥ_temp} H_σ(T) (Plancherel), and archimedeanly H_σ extends continuously to Ψ^{−N}(π), uniformly in π, σ, by (18.5).
items.note: Lemma 18.1(i)–(iii); proof in Appendix A.6, which rests on /65. The convergence (18.1) and the local period for each pair of vectors are /101 (route 2, the GGP roadmap); this item imports them. (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) relative-character.)

items.name: Positivity of relative characters (cited; archimedean case expected)
items.statement: For v ∈ π and u ∈ σ the local period ∫_H⟨sv, v⟩⟨u, su⟩ (/101) is ≥ 0; summing over B(σ), H_σ(v ⊗ v̄) ≥ 0, so H_σ(v) = ‖ℓ_σ(v)‖² for an H-invariant ℓ_σ: π → σ unique up to phase; known for F non-archimedean [SVe].
items.note: Used only through the manifest positivity of global periods (Remark 22.3).

items.name: A-priori bounds for relative characters
items.statement: Let (G, H) be a GGP pair over an archimedean local field, and π, σ tempered. Then H_σ(Op_h(a)) ≪ h^{−N} for a ∈ S^{−∞}_δ, and ≪ h^N⟨hλ_π⟩^{−N}⟨hλ_σ⟩^{−N} unless (hλ_π, hλ_σ) is o(1)-close to the image of supp a.

items.name: Asymptotics of relative characters in the stable case
items.statement: Let (G, H) be a GGP pair over an archimedean local field. Fix compact U ⊆ g^∧ of H-stable elements, 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, a ∈ S^{−∞}_δ(g^∧) supported in U, and h-dependent tempered π, σ. Then H_σ(Op_h(a)) = ∫_{hO_{π,σ}} a + O(h^{1−2δ}); more precisely there are D_j of order ≤ 2j, homogeneous of degree j, D_0 = 1, with H_σ(Op_h(a)) = Σ_{j<J} h^j ∫_{hO_{π,σ}} D_j a + O(h^{(1−2δ)J}), constants Cν(a).
items.note: With (19.9)–(19.11). The proof reduces (§19.4) to Theorem 19.4 for M = G × H, S = diag H, τ = π ⊠ σ̄, whose printed (19.16) omits the factor h^j (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E5). (arXiv v3 Theorem 15; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-15, theorem-16.)

items.name: Small, medium and huge elements of S
items.statement: (Lemma 19.5) ∫ Θ(y/h^{δ′})j_S(y)tr(π(exp y)Op_h(a))dy = Σ_{j<J} h^j ∫_{hO_π∩s⊥} D_j a + O(h^{(1−2δ)J}) for δ < δ′ < 1/2; (Lemma 19.6) ∫_{‖s−1‖≥h^{−N′}} tr(π(s)Op_h(a)) ≪ h^N; (Lemmas 19.7–19.8) for S-stable ω some unit u ∈ m has |s·u| ≍ |(s·u)ω| ≫ ‖s‖^ε, and tr(π(s)Op_h(a)) ≪ h^∞ when ‖s−1‖ ≥ h^{1/2−η}.
items.note: Lemmas 19.5–19.8 and (19.31); the proof of Lemma 19.5 has a normalisation slip (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E6).

items.name: The Plancherel formula for real reductive groups (Harish-Chandra; cited)
items.statement: For G a real reductive group (complex groups included by restriction of scalars) and f ∈ C_c^∞(G), f(1) = ∫_{Ĝ_temp} χ_π(f) for the Plancherel measure dual to dg; for n large in terms of G the formula extends by continuity to n-fold differentiable compactly supported f.
items.note: Harish-Chandra. The archimedean half of §A.3; the p-adic half (Waldspurger) and §A.4.1 are /100. Routed (route 4) to the Part II of AutomorphicSpectralTheory that PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21 route 1 proposes: its item /25 (the L² form on the Schwartz algebra S(G)) is the same theorem, by polarisation ((f₂* ∗ f₁)(1) = ⟨f₁, f₂⟩) and Dixmier–Malliavin. Route 1 imports it; /65 (the extension to Ξ-integrable functions) stays in route 1.

items.name: Plancherel formula for Ξ-integrable functions
items.statement: For f in the space F (all G × G-derivatives in L¹(Ξ dg)) and tempered π, there is a unique continuous π(f): π^∞ → π^∞ with ⟨π(f)u, v⟩ = ∫ f(g)⟨gu, v⟩; f ↦ π(f) is continuous into trace class, ∫‖π(f)‖_1 < ∞, and the Plancherel formula holds on F.
items.note: §A.5 and §A.6 (proof of Lemma 18.1). (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) plancherel-technicalities.)

items.name: Distinguished duals and the functionals ℓ_σ
items.statement: Ĥ^π_temp = {σ tempered: Hom_H(π, σ) ≠ 0}; H_σ ≠ 0 exactly on Ĥ^π_temp for F non-archimedean [BP3, Wll]; ℓ_σ with H_σ(v1 ⊗ v̄2) = ⟨ℓ_σ v1, ℓ_σ v2⟩ (20.1), extended crudely to non-tempered σ; for compact H, π|_H = ⊕ σ and every finitely supported k on Ĥ^π_temp is H_σ(T) for some T (positive definite if k ≥ 0).
items.note: §20 and §21. (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) inverse-branching.)

items.name: Orbit-distinction
items.statement: σ ∈ Ĥ_temp is orbit-distinguished by π if O_{π,σ} ≠ ∅. For hλ_σ in a fixed compact subset of [h^∧] ∩ image(O_stab) and small h, orbit-distinction implies distinction (by Theorem 19.3); the converse is expected.
items.note: Remark 22.1.

items.name: Archimedean inverse branching
items.statement: Let π have limit orbit O, k ∈ C_c^∞([h^∧] ∩ image(O_stab)), k ≥ 0, with U, V as in (22.2)–(22.4); k_h(σ) = k(hλ_σ) for tempered orbit-distinguished σ, else 0. Suppose (22.8): the h-dependent maps H_σ (for non-tempered σ as well) factor as Ψ^{−∞}(π) → Ψ^{−∞}(σ) → C (the second arrow the trace), with the first arrow h-uniformly continuous. For ε > 0, N there are a, a1, a2, a_nt ≥ 0 in C_c^∞(V) with ∫_O a1² dω ≪ 1, ∫_O a2², ∫_O a_nt² ≤ ε, |∫k − ∫_O a² dω| ≤ ε, and for small h: |k_h(σ)| ≤ |H_σ(Op_h(a1)²)|, |k_h(σ) − H_σ(Op_h(a)²)| ≤ |H_σ(Op_h(a2)²)| + O(h^N) for tempered σ with hλ_σ ∈ U, O_{π,σ} ≠ ∅; and H_σ(Op_h(a)²) = H_σ(Op_h(a_nt)²) + O(h^N) for non-tempered σ with hλ_σ ∈ U. The implied constants depend on (N, k, a, ε) but not on (π, σ, h).
items.note: With (22.5)–(22.7) and Remark 22.3; the normalisation (22.8) is a hypothesis. The + O(h^N) in (22.10) is the corrected statement: the printed exact inequality is not proved where hλ_σ ∉ U0, and the proof needs a chosen with the image of its support compact in U0 (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E21); Theorem 30.1 absorbs the O(h^N). (arXiv v3 Theorem 17; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-17.)

items.name: Test functions for the Weyl law
items.statement: For k ≥ 0 as above, ε > 0, N and small h there are positive-definite f, f1 in the Hecke algebra, supported on 1 + o(1), with |∫k − h^d f(1)| ≤ ε, f1(1) ≤ εh^{−d} and |k_h(σ) − χ_σ(f)| ≤ χ_σ(f1) + O(h^N⟨hλ_σ⟩^{−N}) for all σ.

items.name: Good compact open subgroups and invariant vectors
items.statement: For suitable K there are good (normal in K, Iwahori-factorized for every standard parabolic) J_n forming a basis at 1 [MP]; for good J, a supercuspidal τ of M has J_M-fixed vectors iff some (every) subquotient of i^H_P τ has J-fixed vectors.
items.note: Lemmas 23.1–23.2; uses Jacquet's lemma [Cas2, Theorem 3.3.3] and [BZ, §2.13].

items.name: Supercuspidal support and the Bernstein center
items.statement: Each irreducible π is a subquotient of i^H_M τ for a unique class [(M, τ)] with τ supercuspidal (its infinitesimal character); the Bernstein center Z(H) = O(⊔Θ) acts on every smooth representation, by z(λ_π) on irreducibles, and z·v = h_z ∗ v for a central h_z ∈ H^J.
items.note: Lemmas 23.3 and 23.5, §§23.5–23.6; SR.3 plans the Bernstein decomposition and centre.

items.name: Tempered representations from square-integrable ones (cited)
items.statement: Each tempered irreducible π is a submodule of i^H_M σ for a unique class [(M, σ)] with σ square-integrable.
items.note: [Wld, Proposition III.4.1]. Routed (route 5) to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3, which plans the matrix-coefficient criteria for temperedness; PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23 sends the same theorem there (its item rev-langlands-classification-and-harish-chandra (b), route 3). Route 1 imports it.

items.name: l-components
items.statement: The Langlands map l: Ĥ_temp → ⊔D, σ ↦ [(M, τ)] with σ ↪ i^H_M τ, τ square-integrable; l-components D ≅ X^0_M/Γ (compact tori mod finite groups), each mapping continuously to one Bernstein component; only finitely many contain representations with J-fixed vectors.
items.note: §§23.7–23.8; generic irreducibility [Cas2, Theorem 6.6.1].

items.name: Strong multiplicity one (cited) and the structure of Ω
items.statement: l is injective on Ω = Ĥ^π_temp (non-archimedean GGP) and l(Ω) is a union of l-components, so Ω is a union of finite quotients of compact tori on which σ ↦ H_σ is continuous (24.1).
items.note: Lemmas 24.1–24.2 [MW, BP1, BP2, FLO].

items.name: Allowable components and functions
items.statement: An l-component D ⊆ Ω^J is allowable if every non-negative k ∈ C(D) can be approximated: for each ε there are positive-definite T, T₊ ∈ π^J ⊗ π̄^J with tr T₊ ≤ ε and |k(σ) − H_σ(T)| ≤ H_σ(T₊) for all σ ∈ Ĥ, and φ, φ₊ ∈ H^J with φ₊ positive definite and φ₊(1) ≤ ε and |k(σ) − tr σ(φ)| ≤ tr σ(φ₊); k is allowable if supported on finitely many allowable components.
items.note: With Remark 24.4 and (24.7).

items.name: Cuspidal-type components are allowable
items.statement: Every l-component whose inducing data are supercuspidal (e.g. the unramified principal series) is allowable.
items.note: Proof in §§24.4–24.5 (Steps 1–6). (arXiv v3 Theorem 18; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-18.)

items.name: Uniform distinction and the Stone–Weierstrass inputs
items.statement: There is positive-definite T with H_σ(T) ≥ 1 on Ω^J (Lemma 24.6); Θ̄^nt ∩ Θ^0 has measure zero (Lemma 24.8); regular functions on the real form of Θ separate λ(D) from λ(D′) (Lemma 24.9) and give f with |f| ≤ 2 on Θ^unit, f ≥ 1 on Θ^nt and ∫_{Θ^0} f² ≤ ε (Lemma 24.10).
items.note: Lemmas 24.6–24.10, Example 24.7; the example given after Lemma 24.10 does not satisfy it (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E3).

items.name: Stone–Weierstrass, Urysohn and Tietze (used)
items.statement: Real subalgebras of C(X, R) separating points on compact X are dense; disjoint closed sets in a normal space are separated by continuous functions; continuous functions on closed subsets of normal spaces extend.
items.note: Used in Lemmas 24.9–24.10 and 31.3.

items.name: Global setting, Tamagawa measures and assumptions
items.statement: (G, H) a GGP pair over a number field F with smooth models outside a finite set R of places; Tamagawa measures on [G], [H] with K, J of volume 1; a fixed cuspidal Π unramified outside R, Π_R = π ⊗ π′ at a distinguished archimedean q; assumptions: π, π′ tempered; G, H anisotropic ((U_{n+1}, U_n), n ≥ 1, or (SO_{n+1}, SO_n), n ≥ 2), so τ(G) = τ(H) = 2; G_p compact at archimedean p ≠ q; G quasi-split at q and π generic.
items.note: §§25.1–25.3, 25.6–25.7; Example 25.3 (F = Q(√5)) and Remark 25.4. Tamagawa measures are planned in AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2; τ(G) = τ(H) = 2 is cited from Weil and Ono. (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) local-conditions-25-7.)

items.name: The branching coefficient L(Π, Σ)
items.statement: For (Π_R, Σ_R) distinguished and tempered, P(v1⊗v2⊗u1⊗u2) = ∫_{[H]}v1ū1 · ∫_{[H]}v̄2u2 and H = ∫_{H_R}⟨hv1,v2⟩⟨u1, hu2⟩ span the same line when H ≠ 0, and L(Π, Σ) ≥ 0 is defined by P = L(Π, Σ)·H.
items.note: (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) branching-coefficient.)

items.name: The Ichino–Ikeda and N. Harris conjectures (conjectural; cited)
items.statement: Conjecture: if (Π_R, Σ_R) is distinguished and tempered then H ≠ 0 and L(Π, Σ) = 2^{−β} (L^{(R)}(½, Π × Σ^∨)/L^{(R)}(1, Ad, Π × Σ^∨)) ∆_G^{(R)}, with 2^β the order of the component group of the Arthur parameter.
items.note: [II], [HarN]; W. Zhang [Z1] proves the global GGP conjecture under local conditions (all archimedean places split; two split supercuspidal places); the refined formula is Zhang's subsequent paper (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 27 (2014)); within §25.7 these conditions leave essentially (U2, U1) (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E33). Remark 25.2 expects 2^β = τ(G)τ(H) generically (Kottwitz). (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) ichino-ikeda.)

items.name: Limit states
items.statement: For fixed positive T′ ∈ π′ ⊗ π̄′ of trace 1, T ↦ [T] (diagonal restriction of T ⊗ T′) is a positivity-preserving G-equivariant map T_1 → C^∞([G]) with ∫[T] = tr T (Lemma 26.2); [a1,…,ak]_h = h^d[Op_h(a1)⋯Op_h(ak)] is h-uniformly continuous (Lemma 26.3), and along a subsequence converges in C^∞ to G-equivariant [a1⋯ak] with [a, ā] ≥ 0, [a] ≥ 0 for a ≥ 0, and ∫_{[G]}[a] = ∫_O a dω (Theorem 26.4).
items.note: §26.3, Example 26.1, Lemmas 26.2–26.3, Theorem 26.4. (arXiv v3 Theorem 19; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-19, limit-states.)

items.name: Disintegration of limit states
items.statement: There is a G-equivariant ξ ↦ [δ_ξ] from O to probability measures on [G] with ∫_{[G]}[a]Ψ = ∫_O a(ξ)[δ_ξ](Ψ)dω(ξ); each [δ_ξ] is invariant under the centralizer G_ξ.
items.note: (26.9); uses Riesz representation and Radon–Nikodym. (arXiv v3 Theorem 20; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-20.)

items.name: Arzelà–Ascoli and Radon–Nikodym (used)
items.statement: Bounded equicontinuous families of continuous functions on compact spaces are precompact; a measure absolutely continuous with respect to a σ-finite measure has a Radon–Nikodym derivative.
items.note: Used in the proofs of Theorems 26.4–26.5.

items.name: Equidistribution of limit states on [H]
items.statement: Under §25.7, and if (G, H) = (SO3, SO2), then Π ≇ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ), where K = F(√−disc V_H) and θ is the spinor norm: for every a ∈ S(g^∧), (1/τ(H))∫_{[H]}[a] = (1/τ(G))∫_{[G]}[a].
items.note: Without that hypothesis the statement is false: for (SO3, SO2) and Π dihedral for K (Π ≅ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ)) the H-period vanishes for every Σ whose weight at q has one sign, with the components at R∖{q} fixed (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E1; RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/1). Under the hypothesis the paper's proof goes through, since ∫_{[G]}[a]·(η_{K/F}∘θ) = 0. Remark 27.2. (arXiv v3 Theorem 21; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-21.)

items.name: Reduction to G∞⁺-invariance
items.statement: Assume if (G, H) = (SO3, SO2), then Π ≇ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ), where K = F(√−disc V_H) and θ is the spinor norm. If every [δ_ξ] is G∞⁺-invariant then Theorem 27.1 holds; each G∞⁺-orbit on [G]/U has the same measure, using strong approximation for the simply connected cover.
items.note: Lemmas 27.3–27.4; the proof of Lemma 27.3 needs H(A) → G(F)G∞⁺U\G(A) surjective, which fails for (SO3, SO2) (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E1). Without that hypothesis the statement is false: for (SO3, SO2) and Π dihedral for K (Π ≅ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ)) the H-period vanishes for every Σ whose weight at q has one sign, with the components at R∖{q} fixed (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E1; RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/1). Under the hypothesis the image of H(A) has index at most 2, the only character of ε trivial on it is η_{K/F}∘θ, and ∫_{[G]}[a]·(η_{K/F}∘θ) = 0 gives the conclusion. The proof's local claim also fails at a real place where V_H is definite and V is not, even for n − 1 ≥ 3; there Kneser's theorem recovers the conclusion globally.

items.name: Strong approximation (cited)
items.statement: For a simply connected F-group each of whose F-simple factors has non-compact F_q-points, G(F)G(F_q) is dense in G(A).
items.note: [PR, Theorem 7.12].

items.name: Regular nilpotents (Kostant; cited)
items.statement: A nilpotent x ∈ n (b = t ⊕ n a Borel) is regular iff its component along every simple root is non-zero; its centralizer is abelian of dimension rank G.
items.note: [Kos1, Theorem 5.3]; Example 27.6; abelian centralizer [Kur].

items.name: Ratner's measure classification (cited)
items.statement: Let G be a connected real Lie group, Γ a lattice and U a subgroup generated by Ad-unipotent one-parameter subgroups. Every U-invariant ergodic probability measure on Γ\G is the homogeneous measure on a closed orbit xS of a closed connected subgroup S ⊇ U; and every U-invariant probability measure is an integral of U-ergodic ones (ergodic decomposition).
items.note: [Rat]; ergodic decomposition [EW, §8.7]. Applied with G∞ semisimple, Γ cocompact arithmetic and U generated by the exponentials of the centraliser of a regular nilpotent. GN.4 owns unipotent-flow theorems but schedules them only for Oppenheim/Duke-type applications, and its packet has no Ratner node, so the item is missing and routed (route 7) to GN.4, with a request to GN.4 for this generality (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/9). Route 1 imports it. (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) ratner-input.)

items.name: Unipotent-invariant measures are G∞⁺-invariant
items.statement: With G quasi-split at q, G anisotropic, ξ ∈ N_reg with centralizer u and U = ⟨exp u⟩: every (Z(A)·U)-invariant probability measure on [G] is G∞⁺-invariant.
items.note: Lemmas 27.8–27.11 (Zariski closure S is reductive, contains G⁺; strong approximation). (arXiv v3 Theorem 22; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-22.)

items.name: Reductive subgroups containing a regular nilpotent centralizer
items.statement: If G is quasi-split real reductive, S ⊆ G a connected reductive subgroup and s ⊇ g_ξ for a regular nilpotent ξ, then S = G.

items.name: Period formula and Parseval identity
items.statement: P_Σ(T ⊗ T′) = ‖projection to Σ of (T ⊗ T′)|_{[H]}‖² satisfies ∫_{[H]}[T] = Σ_Σ P_Σ(T) (28.3), and P_Σ(T) = L(Π, Σ)H_σ(T)H_{σ′}(T′) when L(Π, Σ) is defined (28.5).
items.note: (28.1)–(28.6), §29.1; spectral decomposition of L²([H]) for compact [H] is planned in AS.4.

items.name: Weak Weyl law and truncated spectral expansion
items.statement: #{Σ: P_Σ ≠ 0, |λ_σ| ≤ x} ≪ x^{O(1)} (29.2); for a ∈ C_c^∞(g^∧) supported over W, ∫_{[H]}[a1⋯ak] = lim h^d Σ_{σ good} P_Σ(Op_h(a1)⋯Op_h(ak)), 'good' excluding hλ_σ ∉ U and tempered σ with hO_σ ∩ W = ∅.
items.note: §29.2 and Theorem 29.1. (arXiv v3 Theorem 23; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-23.)

items.name: Smoothly weighted asymptotic formula
items.statement: Assume if (G, H) = (SO3, SO2), then Π ≇ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ), where K = F(√−disc V_H) and θ is the spinor norm. For k ∈ K = C_c^∞([h^∧] ∩ image(O_stab)) and k′ ∈ K′ (products of arbitrary functions at compact archimedean places and allowable functions at finite p ∈ R): h^d Σ_{σ, σ′ tempered, O_{π,σ} ≠ ∅} L(Π, Σ)k_h(σ)k′(σ′) = (τ(H)/τ(G))∫k∫k′ + o(1).
items.note: §30.2, Definition 30.2, Lemmas 30.3–30.6 (Lemma 30.4 applies (27.1)). Without that hypothesis the statement is false: for (SO3, SO2) and Π dihedral for K (Π ≅ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ)) the H-period vanishes for every Σ whose weight at q has one sign, with the components at R∖{q} fixed (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E1; RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/1). (arXiv v3 Theorem 24; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-24.)

items.name: Summing against approximable weights and sets
items.statement: Assume if (G, H) = (SO3, SO2), then Π ≇ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ), where K = F(√−disc V_H) and θ is the spinor norm. Theorem 30.1 extends to k, k′ approximable by K, K′ (Corollary 31.4), in particular characteristic functions of admissible (nice, allowable) sets (Lemmas 31.3, 31.6), giving h^d Σ_{Σ∈F_h} L(Π, Σ) = (τ(H)/τ(G))vol(U)vol(U′) + o(1) (Corollary 31.8) for the family F_h of Definition 31.7.
items.note: Definitions 31.1–31.2, 31.5, 31.7; Lemma 31.3, Corollary 31.4, Lemma 31.6. Without that hypothesis the statement is false: for (SO3, SO2) and Π dihedral for K (Π ≅ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ)) the H-period vanishes for every Σ whose weight at q has one sign, with the components at R∖{q} fixed (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E1; RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/1).

items.name: Size of the family (Weyl law)
items.statement: h^d|F_h| = τ(H)vol(U)vol(U′) + o(1).
items.note: Via the trace formula on compact [H] with the test functions of Lemma 22.4 and (24.4), (24.6). (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) family-and-conductor.)

items.name: Analytic conductor
items.statement: C(Π, Σ) ≍ |F_h|⁴ for Σ ∈ F_h, since C(Π, Σ) ≍ h^{−ε m_G m_H} and 4 dim B_H = ε m_G m_H (Table 1).

items.name: Main theorem: the averaged Gan–Gross–Prasad period
items.statement: Under the assumptions of §25.7 and if (G, H) = (SO3, SO2), then Π ≇ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ), where K = F(√−disc V_H) and θ is the spinor norm, for admissible U, U′ and the family F_h: (1/|F_h|)Σ_{Σ∈F_h} L(Π, Σ) = 1/τ(G) + o(1) (= 1/2); assuming Conjecture 25.1 (or where it is known), (1/|F_h|)Σ (τ(G)τ(H)/2^β)∆_G^{(R)} L^{(R)}(½, Π×Σ^∨)/L^{(R)}(1, Ad, Π×Σ^∨) = τ(H) + o(1).
items.note: Theorem 1.1 of the introduction. Without that hypothesis the statement is false: for (SO3, SO2) and Π dihedral for K (Π ≅ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ)) the H-period vanishes for every Σ whose weight at q has one sign, with the components at R∖{q} fixed (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E1; RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/1). A one-sided admissible U then gives average 0, not 1/2. (arXiv v3 Theorem 25; supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) theorem-25, main-theorem-informal.)

items.name: Weak subconvexity
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 31.11 (§25.7), for fixed Π and Σ traversing a sequence (in the families F_h) whose archimedean parameters at q tend to ∞ at the same rate, L(Π, Σ) = o(C(Π × Σ)^{1/4}).
items.note: From (31.3) by positivity and slowly shrinking families; §31.4. (1.4) holds in all §25.7 cases, including (SO3, SO2) with Π ≅ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ): there the left side of (27.1) is at most twice the right, which is enough for the upper bound (sourceIssues PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/E1). (supersedes cc-d67081 item(s) weak-subconvexity.)

items.name: The p-adic Plancherel formula (Waldspurger; cited) and finiteness of ∫ dim π^U
items.statement: For G reductive over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic 0 and f ∈ C_c^∞(G), f(1) = ∫_{Ĝ_temp} χ_π(f) for the Plancherel measure dual to dg; hence, for U compact open, ∫_{Ĝ_temp} dim π^U < ∞.
items.note: [Wld] (Harish-Chandra's theorem in Waldspurger's account). Split from /64 (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/5–/6): no stage of the atlas plans the p-adic Plancherel formula (SR.3 does not), so it stays in route 1; a SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups Part II is the alternative owner.

items.name: The local period of a GGP pair and its convergence (18.1)
items.statement: For a GGP pair (G, H) of §13 over a local field (orthogonal, unitary or general linear), ∫_H Ξ_G|_H Ξ_H < ∞ (18.1); hence for tempered irreducible unitary π of G and σ of H and smooth v1, v2 ∈ π, u1, u2 ∈ σ the integral ∫_H ⟨sv1, v2⟩⟨u1, su2⟩ ds converges absolutely and defines an H-invariant form, continuous in the four vectors.
items.note: [II, Proposition 1.1], [HarN, §2]. The unnormalised Ichino–Ikeda/N. Harris local period of π ⊠ σ̄ on the diagonal H ⊂ G × H. The GGP roadmap owns it: PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-CHAUDOUARD-ZYDOR-22/4 defines the normalised period with its convergence for unitary pairs; this item adds the orthogonal and general linear pairs. Split from /59 (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/8); /59 (route 1) and /80 import it.

items.name: Chevalley's restriction theorem and the Harish-Chandra isomorphism for reductive g_C
items.statement: For a reductive Lie algebra g_C = z ⊕ [g_C, g_C] over C with Cartan subalgebra t_C and Weyl group W: restriction C[g*_C]^G → C[t*_C]^W is an isomorphism onto a polynomial ring, so [g*_C] := Spec Sym(g_C)^G ≅ t*_C/W is an affine space (Chevalley); and Harish-Chandra's γ: Z(U(g_C)) ≅ S(t_C)^W ≅ C[[g*_C]] (from the semisimple case on [g_C, g_C] and the centre). For GL_n, [g*_C] is the space of characteristic polynomials (Example 9.1).
items.note: Chevalley, Harish-Chandra; imports LieHighestWeight layers 7 and 9. Nothing in the atlas states Chevalley's restriction theorem, and layer 9 does not treat the centre of U(gl_n). Routed (route 8) to a Part II of LieHighestWeight, merged by the queue into DESIGN-LieHighestWeightPartII, as the single foundational owner (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/10). Route 1 imports it.

items.name: The real form [ig*] and the infinitesimal character λ_π
items.statement: For G real reductive, [ig*] = {λ ∈ [g*_C] : λ = −λ̄} is a real form of [g*_C], cut out by generators of Sym(g_C)^G defined over R; the infinitesimal character λ_π ∈ [g*_C] of a representation π on which Z(U(g_C)) acts by scalars is the point corresponding, under γ (/102), to the character by which Z acts.
items.note: (9.3); §§9.4–9.5 define λ_π. Split from /28 (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/10): it stays in route 1, importing /102.

items.name: Local multiplicity one for GGP pairs (cited)
items.statement: For a GGP pair (G, H) of §13 over a local field of characteristic 0 (orthogonal, unitary or general linear) and irreducible smooth (Casselman–Wallach, archimedeanly) representations π of G and σ of H, dim Hom_H(π, σ) ≤ 1.
items.note: Aizenbud–Gourevitch–Rallis–Schiffmann (p-adic); Sun–Zhu and Aizenbud–Gourevitch (archimedean). Used to define ℓ_σ (Remark 18.2, §20) and the branching coefficient (§25.4). It is the case ℓ = 0 of PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20/bessel-uniqueness, on that paper's accepted route to GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups; its relevant pairs take E = F or a quadratic field, so the general linear case of §13 (k1 = k × k, at split places of the unitary groups) needs AGRS and Sun–Zhu as well (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/11(a)).

items.name: The Schwartz kernel theorem (cited)
items.statement: For manifolds X and Y, every separately continuous bilinear form B: C_c^∞(X) × C_c^∞(Y) → C is B(a, Ψ) = η(a ⊗ Ψ) for a unique distribution η on X × Y; so a form on the algebraic tensor product extends uniquely to C_c^∞(X × Y).
items.note: Applied with X = g^∧ and Y = [G] (compact). Neither library has it (Mathlib's distribution file names it only as a future goal). Routed (route 9) to AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.0, which plans nuclear Fréchet test-function spaces (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/11(b)). Route 1 imports it.

items.name: The Riesz–Markov–Kakutani representation theorem (cited)
items.statement: For a locally compact Hausdorff space X, every positive linear functional Λ on C_c(X, R) is integration against a regular Borel measure µ_Λ: ∫ f dµ_Λ = Λ(f).
items.note: Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/RieszMarkovKakutani/Real.lean (rieszMeasure, line 65; integral_rieszMeasure, line 345); the NNReal version is NNRealRMK.rieszMeasure. Applied to the positive distribution η on g^∧ × [G].

items.name: Spinor norms, determinants and G(F_v)/G(F_v)⁺
items.statement: For a non-degenerate quadratic space V over a field F of characteristic ≠ 2, the spinor norm θ: SO(V)(F) → F^×/F^{×2} has kernel the image of Spin(V)(F). Over a local field F_v, θ is surjective on SO(V) when dim V ≥ 3 and v is finite; for dim V = 2 its image is N(K_v^×)F_v^{×2}, K = F(√−disc V); at a real place its image is determined by the signature. For G = SO(V), θ injects G(F_v)/G(F_v)⁺ into F_v^×/F_v^{×2}; for unitary groups det injects G(F_v)/G(F_v)⁺ into the norm-one elements of (E ⊗ F_v)^× and is surjective on U_{n−1}.
items.note: The locus of sourceIssues E1. Tau Ceti (f790474) has the spinor norm and its kernel: tauceti:CliffordAlgebra.spinorNorm and tauceti:CliffordAlgebra.range_spinToSpecialOrthogonal_eq_ker_spinorNorm ('The image of the Spin action on SO(Q) is exactly the kernel of the spinor norm'), TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/CliffordAlgebra/Spin/SpinorNorm/Basic.lean, lines 213 and 323, over a field with 2 invertible. The local images and the unitary determinant step are missing (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/11(d)).

items.name: The compactness criterion for anisotropic groups (cited)
items.statement: For a reductive group G over a number field F, G(F)\G(A)¹ is compact iff G is F-anisotropic modulo its centre; equivalently, the compactness of [G] forces G(F) to contain no non-trivial unipotent elements.
items.note: Borel–Harish-Chandra, Mostow–Tamagawa. AA.3 proves compactness for F-anisotropic groups modulo centre and states the converse; Lemma 27.8 uses the converse direction (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/11(e)).

items.name: Nelson's theorems on ∆ (cited)
items.statement: For a unitary representation π of a Lie group G and a basis B of g, ∆ = 1 − Σ_{x∈B} x² is essentially self-adjoint on π^∞, its closure is positive with bounded inverse of norm ≤ 1, and π^∞ = ∩_{n≥0} D(∆^n).
items.note: [NS] (Nelson–Stinespring) and [NE, Corollary 9.3] (E. Nelson, Analytic vectors). Item /4 uses these uncited; they underlie every Sobolev statement of Part I (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/11(f)).

items.name: Local finiteness of orbital measures (Ranga Rao; cited)
items.statement: For G real reductive and a coadjoint orbit O ⊂ g^∧ with its normalised symplectic measure ω, ∫_O a dω converges for every a ∈ C_c(g^∧), so ω defines a Radon measure on g^∧.
items.note: [Rao] (Ranga Rao, Ann. of Math. 96 (1972)), in its Lie-algebra form (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/11(g)).

items.name: Uniform admissibility (cited)
items.statement: For G reductive over a non-archimedean local field and J compact open, dim σ^J is bounded uniformly over irreducible smooth σ.
items.note: Bernstein. SR.3a plans exactly this bound B(G, U) (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/11(h), as corrected by its verification).

items.name: Connectedness of simply connected real groups (É. Cartan; cited)
items.statement: For a simply connected semisimple group G^sc over R (and over C), G^sc(R) is topologically connected; hence G^sc(F_q) and G^sc(F_∞) are connected.
items.note: É. Cartan; used to identify the images of G^sc(F_q) and G^sc(F_∞) with connected components (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/11(i)).

items.name: Borel's density theorem (cited)
items.statement: Let S be a closed connected subgroup of a real Lie group and Γ_S ⊂ S a lattice. Then the real points of the Zariski closure of Γ_S contain every unipotent element of S.
items.note: [Mo, Proposition 4.7.1]. Routed (route 7) with Ratner's theorem (/89) to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.4 (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/9 and /11). Route 1 imports it.

coverage.policy: Every numbered definition, lemma, proposition, theorem and corollary is covered, with closely linked statements merged into one item and named in its note; cited theorems the proofs depend on (Kirillov formula, Langlands classification, Plancherel, Ratner, Borel density, GIT, local and strong multiplicity one, the Schwartz kernel and Riesz theorems, spinor norms, Ichino–Ikeda) are items; examples and remarks only where they carry mathematics used later.

routes.title: The orbit method in quantitative form: microlocal analysis on representations of reductive groups
routes.brief: A new roadmap for the local and analytic machinery of Nelson–Venkatesh, The orbit method and analysis of automorphic forms (Acta Math. 226 (2021), 1–209; arXiv:1805.07750): a pseudodifferential calculus for unitary representations of Lie groups in which symbols on g^∧ are quantized to operators Op_h(a) and traces are integrals over coadjoint orbits, applied to Gan–Gross–Prasad restriction problems. Final theorems, as the paper states them (published numbering; arXiv v3 numbers the same theorems 1–24 consecutively): Theorems 4.5, 5.6, 5.8, 7.4, 8.11 (star product, Op(S^m) ⊆ Ψ^m, Op_h(S^m_δ) ⊆ h^{min(0,m)}Ψ^m_δ and the composition expansions, also for pairs g1 + g2 = g); Theorem 6.1 (Rossmann's Kirillov formula, cited) and Theorems 6.3, 12.2 (trace and trace-norm estimates uniform in tempered π); Theorem 11.1 and Lemma 11.6 (limit orbits; a fixed tempered π has non-empty limit orbit in N_reg iff it is generic); Theorems 14.2 and 14.5 (for a GGP pair, H-stability ⇔ ev(x) ∩ ev(x_H) = ∅; stable fibres O^{λ,µ} are H-torsors over an algebraically closed field, and empty or H-torsors over R); Theorems 16.7, 17.2 (compatibility of volume forms and disintegration of orbital measures); Theorem 19.3 (H_σ(Op_h(a)) = Σ_{j<J} h^j ∫_{hO_{π,σ}} D_j a + O(h^{(1−2δ)J}) on compact sets of H-stable elements); Theorem 22.2 and Theorem 24.5 (inverse branching at the distinguished archimedean place and at p-adic places, cuspidal-type l-components being allowable); Theorems 26.4–26.5, 27.1, 27.7 (limit states, their disintegration and equidistribution on [H]); Theorems 29.1 and 30.1 (truncated spectral expansion and the smoothly weighted formula (τ(H)/τ(G))∫k∫k′). Cover in this order: (1) symbol classes, operator classes, the star product and the composition, division and localization lemmas (Parts I–II); (2) coadjoint orbits, infinitesimal characters, the temperedness criterion (Lemma 9.4), limit orbits and trace estimates, with the K-type and Plancherel technicalities of Appendix A; (3) GIT stability for GGP pairs, volume forms and disintegration (§§14, 16–17); (4) relative characters and their stable asymptotics (§§18–19); (5) inverse branching (§§20–24); (6) limit states, Ratner-based equidistribution and the truncated spectral expansion (§§26–30). Keep δ < 1/2 (the Planck scale) and the h-dependent conventions of §1.14 visible. Theorem 27.1 (and Theorems 30.1 and 31.11) is false for (SO3, SO2) with Π dihedral for K = F(√−disc V_H), since the torus's spinor norms are norms from K (sourceIssues E1): state it with the hypothesis Π ≇ Π ⊗ (η_{K/F}∘θ) in that case. Import rather than re-plan: the exponential map, Ad, BCH and KAK from Lie groups and the Lie algebra correspondence (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieGroups, layers 0, 1, 3, 9), whose representation-theory family excludes unitary duals of noncompact groups; the Harish-Chandra isomorphism for semisimple Lie algebras from LieHighestWeight layer 7, and Chevalley's restriction theorem with the Harish-Chandra isomorphism for reductive g_C from the LieHighestWeight Part II proposed in route 8 (the real form [ig*] and λ_π are planned here); (g, K)-modules and infinitesimal characters from AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1–AF.2; trace-class, Hilbert–Schmidt and spectral decomposition from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0 and AS.4; Hecke algebras, induction, admissibility, uniform admissibility (SR.3a), the Bernstein centre and Harish-Chandra's classification of tempered representations (Lemma 23.4, route 5) from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1–SR.3 (and the proposed SmoothRepresentations Part II roadmaps for characters and the unitary dual, where accepted); Tamagawa measures, the compactness criterion for anisotropic groups and strong approximation from AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2, AA.3 and AA.4; Ratner's measure classification, the ergodic decomposition and Borel's density theorem from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 (route 7); GGP pairs, local multiplicity one, the local period ∫_H⟨sv1, v2⟩⟨u1, su2⟩ with its convergence (18.1) and positivity, and the branching coefficient from GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups (this roadmap keeps H_σ as the sum over B(σ), with Lemma 18.1(i)–(iii), because its proof uses Appendix A); the Langlands classification for real reductive groups from AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 (AF.1b once the RT-AREA-automorphic-1 fixes are applied; route 3); Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula for real reductive groups from the Part II of AutomorphicSpectralTheory (route 4), which owns it; affine GIT quotients, the stable locus, the principal-bundle statement [MFK, Proposition 0.9] and the Hilbert–Mumford criterion in its stability form from the Part II of Tau Ceti's Reductive algebraic groups (route 6); the Schwartz kernel theorem from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0 (route 9); the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem from Mathlib (RealRMK.rieszMeasure, RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure); the spinor norm and its kernel from Tau Ceti (CliffordAlgebra.spinorNorm, CliffordAlgebra.range_spinToSpecialOrthogonal_eq_ker_spinorNorm). Cited inputs to plan here: Harish-Chandra's character theory, Rossmann's orbital results, Vogan and Blattner, Cowling–Haagerup–Howe, Kostant and Barbasch–Vogan on generic representations, Waldspurger's p-adic Plancherel formula with ∫ dim π^U < ∞ (no other owner), E. Nelson's and Nelson–Stinespring's theorems on ∆ (π^∞ = ∩D(∆^n)), Ranga Rao's local finiteness of orbital measures, Cartan's connectedness of simply connected real groups, the local images of the spinor norm and of det on unitary groups, and the Cotlar–Stein lemma (strong convergence).

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: good characteristic and coadjoint invariant theory
routes.brief: This route coalesces with the Part II of Tau Ceti's Reductive algebraic groups proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21 (its route 4, accepted), pending as DESIGN-ReductiveGroupsPartIII because ReductiveGroupsPartII exists; keep its id, title, area and brief. That design plans orbit closures, affine semistability and closed orbits (FINTZEN-21 /32) and Kempf's rational destabilising cocharacter (/32a). Nelson–Venkatesh (§14, Lemma 14.1, p. 96, and before (14.2), p. 97) need, for a reductive group H acting on an affine variety M over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0: (1) the categorical quotient φ: M → M//H = Spec k[M]^H, affine, surjective and universal; (2) openness of the stable locus M^s (closed orbit, finite stabiliser) and of φ(M^s); (3) if stabilisers on M^s are trivial, M^s → φ(M^s) is a principal H-bundle, locally trivial in the étale topology [MFK, Proposition 0.9]; (4) the Hilbert–Mumford criterion in its stability form: x is not H-stable iff lim_{t→0} λ(t)x exists for some non-trivial cocharacter λ (for a linear action: λ has only non-negative weights on x). (4) follows from the closed-orbit form (Richardson, Kempf) with Matsushima's theorem (a closed orbit has reductive stabiliser, and an infinite reductive stabiliser contains a non-trivial torus); the null-cone form of /32a does not give it alone. The categorical quotient and Hilbert–Mumford are also sent to LanglandsParameterStacks LP2/LP3 by PAPER-BOCKLE-HARRIS-KHARE-ETAL-19 (route 2, item /4) and PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 (route 3, item /35): choose one owner with the maintainer, and let the other import. QuantitativeOrbitMethodAndMicrolocalAnalysisOnLieGroups imports (1)–(4), applied to H acting linearly on g (Theorem 14.2) and on m (Lemmas 19.7–19.8).

routes.title: Representations of semisimple Lie algebras, highest weight theory, and the Weyl formulas, Part II: Chevalley restriction and the Harish-Chandra isomorphism for reductive Lie algebras
routes.brief: The queue merges this route with the other LieHighestWeight Part II proposals (PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-25, routes 3 and 19) into DESIGN-LieHighestWeightPartII. sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 27.3, p. 182 (also arXiv v3)
sourceIssues.printed: For G=SOn, the source claims that the spinor norm embeds G(Fv)/G(Fv)+ in Fv× modulo squares. It derives the assertion from the spinor norm being surjective on SOn−1 when n−1⩾2.
sourceIssues.correction: For (G, H) = (SO3, SO2) and Π ≅ Π ⊗ χ, where χ := η_{K/F}∘θ, K = F(√−disc V_H) and θ is the spinor norm, Theorem 27.1 and (31.3) of Theorem 31.11 are false, and with them Theorem 30.1 and Corollaries 31.4 and 31.8: with the components σ′ at the places of R∖{q} fixed, the H-period of Π against Σ vanishes identically for every Σ whose archimedean weight at q has one sign (when K_q = C), so a one-sided admissible U gives average 0, not 1/τ(G) = 1/2; and (27.1) fails for suitable a. They fail whenever Π ≅ Π ⊗ χ, also when K splits at q: then the sign depends on σ′ alone, and a suitable singleton U′ gives average 0 or 1. The weak subconvex bound (1.4) still holds, losing at most a factor 2. With the added hypothesis 'if (G, H) = (SO3, SO2), then Π ≇ Π ⊗ χ' the statements hold: χ is then the only character of ε trivial on the image of H(A), and ∫_{[G]}[a]χ = 0 because multiplication by χ carries Π into the orthogonal Π ⊗ χ. Remark: the same sentence also asserts local surjectivity of the spinor norm on SO_{n−1} at every place. That is false at a real place where V_H is definite and V is not (θ(H_q) = 1 while θ(G_q) = {±1}; at q this happens for (SO(2,1), SO(2)) and (SO(3,1), SO(3)), both quasi-split), even when n − 1 ≥ 3. For dim V_H ≥ 3 the conclusion is recovered globally (Kneser: θ(G(F)) = F^× ∩ θ(G(A))), so there only the proof is affected.
sourceIssues.reason: (a) Images. For SO2 = SO(V_H) with V_H an anisotropic plane, θ(SO2(F_v)) = N(K_v^×)F_v^{×2}, of index 2 in F_v^×/F_v^{×2} wherever K_v is a field. The spinor norms of G(F)H(A)G(A)⁺ lie in F^×N(A_K^×)(A^×)² = ker η_{K/F}, while θ(SO3(F_v)) = F_v^×/F_v^{×2}. So χ is a non-trivial automorphic character of G(A), trivial on G(F), H(A) and G(A)⁺, and non-trivial on ε = G(F)G∞⁺U\G(A) once θ(U) ⊆ ker η_{K/F}. Then the image of H(A) in ε is ker χ, of index 2, and (27.1) ⟺ ∫_{[G]}[a]χ = 0. (b) Example. F = Q, D an indefinite quaternion division algebra, G = PD^× = SO(D⁰, Nrd), K ⊂ D imaginary quadratic, H = K^×/Q^× = SO(K^⊥ ∩ D⁰), so χ = η_K∘Nrd. Π = JL(π(ψ)) for a Hecke character ψ of K with ψ|_{A^×} = η_K (trivial central character), D ramified only at primes where π(ψ) is supercuspidal (these are non-split in K, so K embeds in D), and Π_∞ = D_k with k even, tempered and generic as §25.7 requires. Then Π ⊗ χ ≅ Π. (c) Vanishing. χ is trivial on H(A), so ∫_{[H]}φΣ̄ = ∫_{[H]}(χφ)Σ̄. By multiplicity one, multiplication by χ is an involution M = ⊗M_v of Π. M_∞ commutes with PGL₂(R)⁺ and anticommutes with diag(1, −1), which swaps D_k^±, so M_∞ = c·sgn(n) on SO(2)-weight n; at finite v toric multiplicity one (Tunnell–Saito) gives ℓ_v∘M_v = ±ℓ_v, with a sign independent of Σ outside R (at split v, χ_v = 1; at inert v, Σ_v is trivial). Hence, with σ′ fixed, the global H-period vanishes for every Σ of one sign of weight at q, and L(Π, Σ) = 0 by (25.1). Taking the finite places of R non-split in K (single supercuspidal points, allowable by Theorem 24.5) and U a nice interval on the vanishing side of [h^∧] ∩ image(O_stab) = R∖{0}, F_h is non-empty (Lemma 31.9) and every term of (31.3) is 0. Directly, with T′ = u ⊗ ū for an M′-eigenvector u, ∫_{[G]}[a]χ = ±c(∫_{O⁺}a − ∫_{O⁻}a), non-zero for a supported near one sheet of the nilcone. This matches the root numbers: flipping the sign of the weight multiplies the archimedean root number of L(½, ψΩ)L(½, ψ^cΩ) by −1. (d) (1.4). [a] ⩾ 0 and ε/im H(A) injects into A^×/Q^×N(A_K^×) ≅ Z/2 (Kneser for dim V = 3), so the left side of (27.1) is at most twice the right, and the upper-bound half of the argument gives L(Π, Σ) = o(C^{1/4}). The counterexample is RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21/1, checked step by step in its verification (RT-PAPER-NELSON-VENKATESH-21.review.json).
